title: What If You Fell Into Jupiter? You'd Sink for 78 Days
alt_titles: What Happens If You Fall Into Jupiter?
You Fall Into Jupiter at 210,000 km/h. Where Do You Stop?
description:
What if you fell into Jupiter? Falling into Jupiter from 1 million km, you hit the clouds at 210,000 km/h, then sink through every layer inside Jupiter: ammonia, rust-colored and water clouds, past the depth where NASA's Galileo probe went silent, into an ocean of hydrogen. Jupiter has no surface, so where do you actually stop?

In this video:
• How fast you hit Jupiter if you fall from far away, and how long the fall takes
• Why an unprotected entry is fatal, compared with NASA's Galileo probe
• Jupiter's three cloud layers, its lightning and its room-temperature level
• What lies below the deepest point any probe has reached
• Where you finally stop inside a planet with no surface, and why

⏱ Chapters
0:00 No Ground
0:10 The Long Drop
1:18 Entry
2:22 The White Ceiling
3:20 The Rust Layer
3:47 The Storm Floor
4:38 Room Temperature
5:07 The Last Signal
5:37 Black Heat
6:17 The Hydrogen Ocean
7:07 Suspended
7:51 No Floor at All

🧮 Key numbers
• Arrival speed from 1 million km: about 57 km/s after 27 hours of falling
• Entry energy: about 390 kg of TNT for every kilogram of you
• Galileo probe: more than 200 g on entry, data for 58 minutes
• Room temperature about 65 km below the 1-bar level (simple adiabat model)
• Neutral buoyancy about 14,000 km down, after about 78 days of sinking (index-1 polytrope model)

Assumptions: you start at rest 1,000,000 km from Jupiter's centre; after the entry you ride an indestructible human-sized pod with the density of a human body. Upper atmosphere: ideal-gas dry adiabat (about); interior: index-1 polytrope (a simple model). Depths are measured below the 1-bar level. Layer boundaries in the cutaway are schematic.

How this was made: the narration is an AI voice (text-to-speech), the script and visuals are made with AI tools and code, and the music and sound effects are synthesised in code. Every number is computed in code from the sources above and fact-checked before upload.
